chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: Annapolis summer job with trumpeter Roosevelt Williams and Oswald Gibson
summary: Before sixteen he goes to Annapolis for a month's club job and discovers he cannot really read music, especially an act's chordless Butterbeans and Susie parts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Anyway, I worked at that job... I think it lasted up into

the summer -- into the summer, I believe. And this was just before my sixteenth birthday. I guess it was about the middle of the summer. One of the fellows who had been playing in Booker Coleman's band had left the band, and went to... I think he had gotten this job in Annapolis, Maryland. And the next thing I knew, he was coming to my house saying that he wanted me to go to Annapolis with him, which was a long ways away to actually travel and play a job. That was just like going to heaven, you know. I really knew I was a big-time musician then.

His name was Roosevelt Williams, a trumpet player. He had been coming to these jam sessions that I had been playing up there... Anyway, he took me. As I said, it was just before my sixteenth birthday. And he had another kid that was about 14 then, and he played saxophone and clarinet. His name was Oswald Gibson. And he took us down to Annapolis, Maryland, and I think we spent the month of August down there -- probably the latter part of July and August, until school opened again.

But that was another great experience. Down there I ran into situations of having to learn pieces fast. Down there was when I really realized that I couldn't read. You know, I knew what reading was about, but I had never had the experience of actually sitting up reading a piece of music --

especially if it didn't have the chords written on there, you know. All of the music had the chords and everything that we had to play, except one of the pieces, and that was something that was sort of a team who were imitating one of the very popular acts of that particular time, a team called Butterbeans and Susie. Well, this wasn't Butterbeans and Susie, but they had a similar type act, and they were using the music of Butterbeans and Susie. And this music did not have any chords on it at all. So I didn't know what to do. Anyway, one of the principals in the show sat down with me, and I caught as much of it as I could by ear...
